title: 2.5 Renowned Taxonomists
description: Carl Linnaeus, Ethiopian taxonomists, and their contributions to biological classification

questions.question: Carl Linnaeus is best known for developing which system?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus created the system of binomial nomenclature (two-part scientific names) and the hierarchical classification system.

questions.question: What is the title often given to Carl Linnaeus?
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus is known as the Father of Taxonomy for his foundational work in classifying and naming organisms.

questions.question: In which century did Carl Linnaeus live?
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus lived from 1707 to 1778, which was the 18th century.

questions.question: What was the title of Carl Linnaeus's major work on plant classification?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus's Species Plantarum (1753) is considered the starting point of botanical nomenclature, listing all known plant species.

questions.question: What was the title of Linnaeus's comprehensive work that classified animals, plants, and minerals?
questions.explanation: Systema Naturae (1735) was Linnaeus's influential work that classified the three kingdoms of nature: animals, plants, and minerals.

questions.question: Before Linnaeus, what method was commonly used to name organisms?
options: Polynomial names with many descriptive words
questions.correctAnswer: Polynomial names with many descriptive words
questions.explanation: Before Linnaeus, organisms were given long polynomial names (many words describing features), which were inconsistent and cumbersome.

questions.question: Linnaeus classified organisms primarily based on:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus used visible physical characteristics (morphology) such as flower parts, body structures, and reproductive organs to classify organisms.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian taxonomist contributed significantly to the study of Ethiopian plant species?
questions.explanation: Abebe Getahun, Tesfaye Awas, and Sebsebe Demissew are prominent Ethiopian botanists who have contributed to plant taxonomy.

questions.question: Professor Sebsebe Demissew is known for his work on:
questions.explanation: Sebsebe Demissew is a renowned Ethiopian botanist who has extensively studied and classified Ethiopian plants.

questions.question: Which international award did Professor Sebsebe Demissew receive for his botanical work?
questions.explanation: Professor Sebsebe Demissew was awarded the prestigious Linnean Medal in 2019 for his contributions to botany.

questions.question: Linnaeus's classification system was based on which feature for plants?
options: Flower parts and reproductive structures (stamens and pistils)
questions.correctAnswer: Flower parts and reproductive structures (stamens and pistils)
questions.explanation: Linnaeus classified plants based on the number and arrangement of their reproductive parts, particularly stamens and pistils.

questions.question: What language did Linnaeus use for his scientific naming system?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus used Latin for scientific names because it was the universal language of scholars in Europe at the time.

questions.question: How did Linnaeus group animals in his classification system?
options: By features such as body structure, number of limbs, and method of reproduction
questions.correctAnswer: By features such as body structure, number of limbs, and method of reproduction
questions.explanation: Linnaeus classified animals based on observable physical characteristics and reproductive methods.

questions.question: The Linnaean system is considered a:
options: Artificial classification system based on observable features
questions.correctAnswer: Artificial classification system based on observable features
questions.explanation: Linnaeus's system is called artificial because it groups organisms based on a few selected physical features rather than evolutionary relationships.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian taxonomist has studied the flora of the Simien Mountains extensively?
questions.explanation: Ensermu Kelbessa is an Ethiopian botanist known for his work on the flora of the Simien Mountains and other regions.

questions.question: Linnaeus divided the natural world into three kingdoms. Which one was NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus originally classified the natural world into three kingdoms: Animalia, Plantae, and Mineralia. Fungi were placed within Plantae.

questions.question: What is the standard abbreviation for Carl Linnaeus in botanical citations?
questions.explanation: In botanical nomenclature, Linnaeus is abbreviated as 'L.' after the scientific names of plants he first described.

questions.question: Linnaeus developed his classification system during which period of scientific history?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus worked during the 18th-century Age of Enlightenment, a period of systematic scientific exploration and classification.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian taxonomist contributed to the Flora of Ethiopia and Eritrea project?
questions.explanation: Many Ethiopian taxonomists including Sebsebe Demissew, Tesfaye Awas, and Ensermu Kelbessa contributed to the Flora of Ethiopia and Eritrea project.

questions.question: The Flora of Ethiopia and Eritrea project documented how many plant species?
questions.explanation: The Flora of Ethiopia and Eritrea project documented approximately 6,000 species of vascular plants found in Ethiopia and Eritrea.

questions.question: Linnaeus believed that species were:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus held a creationist view that species were divinely created and fixed, a view later challenged by evolutionary theory.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of the Linnaean classification system?
options: It does not reflect evolutionary relationships
questions.correctAnswer: It does not reflect evolutionary relationships
questions.explanation: Linnaeus's system groups organisms by physical similarity rather than evolutionary ancestry, which modern cladistics improves upon.

questions.question: Linnaeus's original classification of humans placed them in which group?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus originally placed humans in the order Anthropomorpha (meaning man-like), alongside monkeys and apes, later renamed Primates.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian scientist has contributed to the taxonomy of Ethiopian coffee varieties?
questions.explanation: Taye Kufa is an Ethiopian scientist who has researched and classified the diverse coffee varieties found in Ethiopia.

questions.question: Linnaeus described approximately how many species during his lifetime?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus described and named about 7,700 plant species and 4,400 animal species during his career.
